title: Dabur — Depth & Specificity Research
content:
Dabur's flagship projects and products include a diverse range of categories such as health supplements, digestives, baby care, natural cures, hair care, skin care, oral care, and foods. The company is a leader in Ayurvedic and herbal products, with Dabur Chyawanprash holding a 65% market share in Ayurvedic medicine and Hajmola tablets commanding 75% of the digestive tablets category. Dabur's Vatika brand, including Vatika Hair Oil & Shampoo, has a high growth trajectory, and its honey product has over 40% market share in the branded honey market. Dabur also expanded its portfolio with Menz shampoo, black seed oil & shea butter hair cream under Vatika, and introduced Dabur herbal charcoal toothpaste. The company's flagship brands include Dabur, Vatika, Hajmola, Réal, and Fem, which cover natural healthcare products, premium personal care, digestives, fruit juices and beverages, and fairness bleaches and skin care products respectively.

However, healthcare remained to be the prime-focus for the company and it is the 2nd largest SBU with 28% share in sales [...] Dabur captured the imagination of young Indian consumers in 1996, with the launch of Real Fruit Juices - a new concept in the Indian foods market. The first local brand of 100% pure natural fruit juices made to international standards, Real became the fastest growing and largest selling brand in the country. Subsequently, Dabur Foods also took the route of ethnic cooking pastes and chutneys to enter Indian kitchens – when Hommade was born.

Over the year, Dabur expanded its portfolio to include Menz shampoo, black seed oil & shea butter hair cream under its flagship brand of Vatika and further expanded the oral care portfolio with the introduction of Dabur herbal charcoal toothpaste. To enhance consumer connectivity to its brands, Dabur Egypt upgraded most of its product packaging, giving its products a refreshed look and feel. [...] Dabur has been leading the category growth and is today the number two player in the dentifrice market with its highly differentiated product offerings like the Ayurvedic Dabur Red Paste, herbal offerings like Dabur Babool and Meswak and the newly introduced range of Alpha ingredient products under the Dabur Herb’l brand. The newest addition to the portfolio has been Dabur Red Bae Fresh Gel which has received an encouraging response. Dabur also operates in the toothpowder market with its Dabur [...] Highlights of the Year: Dabur Hajmola ● Hajmola extended its product portfolio with the launch of Mr. Aam variant.
Digestives India's growing population and increasing awareness of digestive health have led to a surge in demand for digestive and intestinal remedies, particularly those based on the principles of Ayurveda. Dabur operates in the herbal digestive category with a portfolio of products under brands like Hajmola, PudinHara, Hingoli, Dabur Nature Care and Sat Isabgol.

Dabur’s FMCG portfolio today includes five flagship brands with distinct brand identities - Dabur as the master brand for natural healthcare products; Vatika for premium personal care; Hajmola for digestives; Réal for fruit juices and beverages; and Fem for fairness bleaches and skin care products. [...] Dabur has conducted detailed Life Cycle Analysis study for three key products – Dabur Chyawanprash, Dabur Honey and Réal to identify risks and opportunities along the entire value chain and, identify steps to be taken to reduce the environment impact of these products. This, we believe, will help further enhance our environmental responsibility efforts. [...] To reduce the impact of our products on the environment, we have conducted the Life Cycle Analysis study for three key products – Dabur Chyawanprash, Dabur Honey and Réal. Further, we have undertaken mass tree plantation at our units and their neighbouring areas.

Dabur's pricing model in the D2C market leverages science-based Ayurveda messaging to enable price premiums in select healthcare SKUs, with certain Ayurvedic health products achieving up to 10–15% higher ASPs versus non-Ayurvedic peers in 2024–25 retail audits. The company positions its products as natural yet clinically validated, aiming to support a price premium in health categories by blending 5,000-year-old wisdom with 21st-century clinical validation.

Dabur responds to D2C disruption by highlighting heritage and quality-control disclosures; third-party validations drove a 2025 brand-trust award tally across India.

### Faster Product and Commercial Testing

Retail environments limit experimentation. D2C removes that barrier.

Brands can validate:

 New product concepts
 Bundles and pricing structures
 Market demand before international expansion

This reduces risk and shortens decision cycles. [...] A direct to consumer model allows brands to sell directly to customers through their own ecommerce platform, while owning pricing, data, and the full customer experience. When positioned correctly, it works alongside retail and marketplace channels rather than competing with them.

Below, we break down the real benefits of D2C, the strategic reasons brands adopt it, and the questions every leadership team should ask before committing resources. [...] Why D2C Is Critical for Brand Control and Growth)

## Three Strategic Reasons Brands Invest in D2C

Beyond operational benefits, these are the strategic reasons D2C becomes a priority.

### Control Over Brand, Pricing, and Experience

No other channel gives brands the same level of control.

You define how products are positioned, how promotions are executed, and how customers interact with your brand. Every touchpoint is consistent and intentional.

Dabur targets a broad demographic across all ages, income levels, and family life stages, including kids, mothers, the elderly, and consumers from lower, middle, and upper class backgrounds. Geographically, Dabur focuses on both domestic and international markets, with a significant emphasis on rural areas domestically and a presence in over 120 countries internationally. The company also has a strong foothold in urban and rural markets, with a focus on Caribbean and Canadian markets for future geographic expansion. Additionally, Dabur has made efforts to penetrate Arab households, particularly in Saudi Arabia, and continues to cater to South Asian consumers in North America while expanding to multi-ethnic consumers.

Dabur's key differentiators compared to other D2C companies include its diversified product portfolio across FMCG, paperboards, packaging, agri-business, and IT, and its focus on Ayurvedic-based beauty and wellness products sold directly to consumers. It also operates internet-first brands like Khetika for dry fruits and ready-to-cook products, and Cavinkare for multicategory convenience food products. Dabur's direct-to-consumer approach allows for stronger brand loyalty and customer relationships, driven by targeted marketing campaigns and better service and support.

Each one moves cost and control between the brand and its partners. A brand that goes direct gains control on all six but also takes on the work a retailer used to do.

### 1. Distribution channels [...] | Price control | Brand sets the selling price | Retailer sets the shelf price; brand can only suggest |

Stronger brand loyalty: In D2C companies, manufacturers have more autonomy in terms of providing consumers with better service and support. This engagement drives strong relationships and retention through targeted marketing campaigns. And in turn, loyal customers yield higher conversion rates. [...] Except for one of the letters, D2C and B2C sound similar enough. They are processes to get products to consumers, which is the ultimate objective of businesses. But as a marketing strategy and a customer journey, D2C/DTC e-commerce, or Direct-to-Consumer e-commerce, has pronounced differences from B2C, or Business-to-Consumer.

  

### What is D2C e-commerce?

Foremost, D2C means the product reaches the consumer directly via digital channels without a middle distribution channel.
